synthesis: Rewrote six original student-visible sections around the governance problem and institutional sequence from Western Zhou enfeoffment through Qin commanderies/counties to early Han parallel commanderies and kingdoms. Instruction explicitly separates chronology from causation, compares continuity/change, traces state capacity and local impact, and marks limits of institutional summaries. Three school plans support common long-period state/society history while differing in emphasis: Nani includes fiscal/selection institutions, Kang Hsuan organizes feudal decline to Qin centralization, and Hanlin foregrounds East Asian and cultural interaction. These are school-plan differences, not claims about publisher textbook text. Original practice cards are labeled as authored paraphrase, not historical quotations.
